chunks.text: The Spread operator, represented by three dots, allows you to spread or expand an iterable

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: such as an array, a string or even an object into its individual elements.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: The spread operator can be used in function calls, array literals and object literals.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: Here's the basic syntax for using it in a function call.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: We have our iterable object and we just add the dot dot dot at the beginning.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: In this example we're adding up some numbers.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: To pass our numbers to the function we use the spread operator.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: The function only accepts the first three elements.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: So if our array were to have more than three, the function would ignore everything after

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: the third.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: Here's the basic syntax for using the spread operator with array literals or strings.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: In this example we can easily combine and organize arrays.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: To accomplish this without using spread we would have to use methods like push, splice,

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: concat, etc.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: We can also spread out the characters of a string into an array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: One of the best cases to use the spread operator is to make a copy of an array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: This comes in very handy when you're using a framework like React.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: We could make a copy of the array by making the new variable equal to the original.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: But this is not really a copy.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: Arrays are reference types.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: So both of these are actually linked to the same data.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: So now if we were to update the copy by pushing something into it, we see that not only is

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: the copy updated, but the original is as well.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: So to make a proper copy of this array, we can use the spread operator.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: Now when we update the copy, the original remains unchanged.

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
chunks.text: Note that spread only does a shallow copy of the array, which means that it only goes

chunks.title: JavaScript Spread Operator
